ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the upper left end is terminal a, and the lower left end is terminal b. Terminal a first connects through a resistor labeled 1Ω to the upper middle node. This middle node connects to the right through a 4Ω resistor to the upper right node, and the upper right node then connects through the vertical 2Ω resistor on the right side to the lower right node. The middle node also connects through a vertical 6Ω resistor to the bottom wire; meanwhile, from the middle node there is an obliquely downward ideal wire directly connected to the lower right node. The bottom wire connects the lower right node and terminal b to the same node. Reasoning: Since there is an ideal wire between the middle node and the lower right node, their potentials are the same and they should be merged into the same node; and the lower right node is also connected to b through the bottom wire, so the middle node is actually node b. Therefore, the 6Ω branch from the middle node to b is bypassed by this short-circuit wire; the 4Ω and 2Ω series branch on the right is also connected between the same shorted node, and likewise does not affect the a-b equivalent resistance. In the end, only the 1Ω resistor remains between a and b, so R_ab = 1Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the image topology: locate a, b, the 1Ω resistor from a to the central node, the diagonal wire from the central node to the bottom b node, and the 6Ω, 4Ω, and 2Ω resistors connected around that short. Then merge the central node with the bottom node because of the diagonal ideal wire. Conclude that the 6Ω branch and the 4Ω+2Ω branch are bypassed by the short, leaving only the 1Ω resistor between a and b. Therefore compute R_ab as 1Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the image and label nodes: take b and the bottom wire as reference; because the diagonal wire connects the central junction directly to the bottom-right/bottom wire, the central junction is also at b potential.
